title: Chapter 8
text: ∫ I do not always hate the cat that kills the bird, only the cat that kills me . . . friend moon, friend cat, you ask no mercy or gigs or gifts, only lull and lavender. and houses. brush. movement as in a bowl. oh young men of Princeton puffing pipes oh young men of Harvard puffing scratching books for security, for friend moon, friend cat you have no justification you are just pink puffs and pastels clouds useless as my girlfriend’s underwear upon the floor or my girlfriend upon the floor puffing for explosion like Ottorino Respighi’s Pines of Rome . . . . tree fulla birds makes justice. or ground fulla worms. or people fulla ground. justification. we walk upon a midnight’s rug neither drunk nor dreamed nor drugged. and when the window bangs down with the hauter and fart of the cannon or the honk puffs the horn like a phallus or the rhinoceros roars in his ice cream dream, roars like the hair on your arm putting down the needle on Kabalevsky’s The Comedians as dimes begin to breathe and Poor ol’ Dolores Costello is rolled up on an old reel in the closet like fishstring. I’m with you . . . friend moon and cat: we turn an ear, an eye, calm in their story, then move on, moon and cat past the old maid’s burning past Van Goghs and Rembrandts hanging like leaves . . . to the top of the roof, tonight; to continents of exactness, to the sound that spins the world.
